source.title: Transcending Scaling Laws with 0.1% Extra Compute
source.authors: Yi Tay; Jason Wei; Hyung Won Chung; Vinh Q. Tran; David R. So; Siamak Shakeri; Xavier García; H. Zheng; J. Rao; A. Chowdhery; Denny Zhou; Donald Metzler; Slav Petrov; N. Houlsby; Quoc V. Le; Mostafa Dehghani

record.file_problem: none; full paper text is present
record.tranche_reason: Tests downstream performance across training compute/checkpoints, using downstream task scores rather than held-out pretraining cross-entropy.
record.gate_note: The paper states that loss under UL2 and causal language modeling is not comparable, and evaluates downstream metrics instead. I record the reported aggregate scaling results relevant to V6. Single-scale benchmark comparisons and qualitative examples do not establish a performance-versus-scale trend; cited scaling-law findings are not this study's results.
record.test_reason: This is mainly a method paper. UL2R continued training is compared against PaLM. As a by-product it reports PaLM's own downstream aggregate score at successive training checkpoints (540B: 182B, 329B, 780B tokens; 8B: plotted curve). That bears weakly on V6, downstream improvement with compute. There is no fit, no extrapolation and no link to pretraining loss. The authors say UL2 and causal-LM losses are not comparable.
record.authors_conclusion: Mostly correct. The authors conclude that UL2R (about 0.1% extra compute) improves PaLM's downstream scaling curves, giving about 2x compute savings at 540B (about 4.4M TPUv4 hours). U-PaLM beats PaLM on English NLP, chain-of-thought reasoning, multilingual tasks, MMLU and BIG-Bench, and gains infilling abilities. The call for downstream metrics in scaling studies appears in the related-work section, not the conclusion.
record.recipe_differences: Continues PaLM training using UL2's mixture-of-denoisers objective and evaluates downstream few-shot task aggregates versus compute; it does not use the original held-out cross-entropy measurement.
record.method_sensitivity: The reported benefit varies with model size and training stage: the 8B advantage narrows near plateau, while the 540B gain continues to grow at the reported 780B-token checkpoint. The authors also say savings depend on training point and convergence stage.

fits_no_version.finding: Continuing PaLM with a different objective (UL2 mixture-of-denoisers, about 0.1–0.16% extra compute) shifts the downstream-score-versus-FLOPs curve. The authors report about 2–2.35x compute savings at 540B; savings at 8B are largest mid-training and smallest at start and convergence.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: The downstream score-versus-compute curve depends on the training objective; a brief change of objective can shift it substantially.

record.peer_reviewed: Conference on Empirical Methods in Natural Language Processing
record.problems: The scaling evidence for V6 uses downstream aggregate benchmark scores, not held-out cross-entropy. The 8B curve is reported in a plot rather than tabulated; the reported aggregate results provide only three 540B checkpoint levels, with no uncertainty estimates or formal predictive-fit evaluation.
record.rows_left_out: Single-scale benchmark tables in Sections 4.2–4.4 were not included because they do not report a scaling trajectory. Figure 2's 540B curve is represented by the more fully specified aggregate results in Appendix 7.1, Table 8.

untested.parts: Held-out pretraining loss versus parameters, tokens or compute; no loss values are reported.
No fits on small runs and no extrapolation.
Effect of shape at fixed parameter count is not studied.
No other modalities; no power-law fits for the continued-training regime.
Predictability: no fitted relation or forecast. Relation to pretraining loss is not tested. Scaling across parameter count is only in BBES plots of tasks selected for emergence.
No exponent fitting or comparison of fitting choices.

missing.what: PaLM 8B downstream aggregate over 7 intermediate checkpoints. The curve rises and then plateaus; values are figure only.
BBES scaling plots across PaLM 8B/62B/540B, GPT-3 and Gopher sizes. Tasks were selected for flat-then-jump behaviour, so they are selection-biased evidence on predictability.

record.verdict_notes: V6 evidence is thin and incidental: three checkpoints of one run, measured in tokens rather than parameters, with no predictive fit. The claim that savings 'can probably be predicted by standard scaling laws' is speculation, not a result. The BBES 'emergence' results rest on tasks chosen for emergent behaviour, so they should not count against V6 predictability without caveat.

versions.untested_parts: Held-out cross-entropy power laws in parameters, tokens, or compute.
Prediction of much larger runs from power laws fitted on smaller runs.
Compute-optimal parameter/token allocation and its trend with compute.
Effects of depth, width, or other architecture details at fixed parameter count.
Power-law scaling in other modalities, repeated-data regimes, fine-tuning, or transfer.
The study reports downstream scores over training checkpoints, but does not fit or validate a predictive relation to pretraining loss or report formal extrapolation from smaller runs.
It does not test how fitting choices affect scaling exponents or compute-optimal splits, nor whether curves bend away from power laws.

rows.subject: U-PaLM 8B
rows.stage_stated: continued training from PaLM checkpoints with UL2R
rows.operation_detail: Compared downstream aggregate scores across training-compute checkpoints for PaLM and U-PaLM.

conditions.value: multiple intermediate checkpoints; 7 U-PaLM training points
average score on 26 zero- and few-shot NLP tasks

rows.measure: Average zero-/few-shot score on NLP tasks versus training FLOPs
rows.note: The authors say UL2R improves the scaling curve, with the gap narrowing as PaLM 8B approaches a plateau and the largest gains occurring around the middle of training.
rows.check: Figure-only comparison of U-PaLM 8B against PaLM 8B, i.e. the study's own method versus its baseline. The V6-relevant content is the PaLM 8B curve alone (rising, then plateauing), which this row does not isolate.

rows.subject: PaLM 540B
rows.operation_detail: Measured the mean aggregate downstream score at successive training-token checkpoints.
rows.note: The paper reports this as the PaLM 540B score at the 182B-token checkpoint.
rows.check: Single checkpoint value (62.7 at 182B tokens). It bears on V6 only as part of the r2–r4 series within one 540B run.

rows.subject: PaLM 540B

relationships.condition: PaLM 540B, single run, three token checkpoints, 26-task zero/one-shot aggregate
relationships.reason: The aggregate score rises monotonically with training tokens: 62.7 to 63.8 to 66.5 (r2–r4). Only three points, with no fit or uncertainty.
relationships.display_finding: The aggregate score increased 62.7→63.8→66.5 across three checkpoints, without a fitted curve or reported uncertainty.

source_check.scope: Only the listed rows, labels and statements were checked; presence is not whole-study approval.
